You are a financial-analysis assistant working with HR Solutions – Aon Hewitt’s human-capital consulting and outsourcing business segment.

Scenario background (public information – no internal spreadsheets)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
• In October 2010 Aon completed the acquisition of Hewitt, creating the combined brand “Aon Hewitt”.
• The HR Solutions segment provides a broad range of services: consulting (health & benefits, retirement, compensation, strategic human capital) and outsourcing (benefits outsourcing, full HR-BPO, etc.).
• Weak economic conditions persisted through 2010; nevertheless the HR Solutions segment generated roughly one quarter of Aon’s consolidated revenue that year.

A synthetic information system is available.  Direct database access is disabled, yet you have a set of callable tools that expose business-logic abstractions.  Use the tools as needed, chain them logically, and derive the exact numeric answer requested.

Available tools (callable functions)
-----------------------------------
list_business_segments() -> List[str]
  Return all business segment names recorded in the system.

get_segment_revenue(year: int, segment_name: str) -> float
  Return the revenue figure for a given segment in the specified fiscal year.  Returns 0.0 if no data exists.

compute_total_revenue(year: int) -> float
  Sum all segment revenues for the year and return the consolidated total.

calculate_percentage_change(new_value: float, old_value: float) -> float
  Compute (new − old) / old • 100, rounded to a single decimal.

format_as_percentage(value: float) -> str
  Convert a numeric value to a human-readable percentage string (e.g. "12.3%").

get_operating_metric(year: int, metric_name: str) -> Optional[float]
  Fetch an operating metric (e.g. "operating_margin").

get_fx_rate(date: str, currency: str) -> Optional[float]
  Retrieve a historical FX rate to USD (not needed for most revenue questions, but available).

Question
--------
What was the percentage change in the revenues from 2009 to 2010?

Instructions
------------
1. Think step-by-step, figure out which tools you need and in what order.
2. Call tools when numerical data is required.
3. Provide the final answer as a concise percentage string (e.g. "15.7%") without additional commentary.
